headline: A billing-blocking CSV export failure following the 4.2 release took 16 days to resolve due to inaccurate priority classification, uncoordinated commitments by account management, an OOO handover gap, and unverified release confirmations to the client.

actors.name: Hannah Lee
actors.summary: Reported and followed up on failing scheduled warehouse CSV export.

actors.name: Minh Tran
actors.summary: Handled support ticket SUP-4812, provided manual workarounds, and maintained support updates.

actors.name: Ravi Kumar
actors.summary: Investigated root cause, resolved DST test failures, and deployed export fix in 4.2.4.

actors.name: Sarah Okafor
actors.summary: Promised unverified fix timeline, failed to reprioritize ticket, and omitted issue from OOO handover.

actors.name: Tom Becker
actors.summary: Covered for Sarah during leave and incorrectly informed the client that the fix had deployed in 4.2.3.

actors.name: Priya Shah
actors.summary: Managed release cycles 4.2.3 and 4.2.4, pulling the export PR from 4.2.3 due to integration test failure.

actors.name: Daniel Reyes
actors.summary: Escalated prolonged failure and conflicting communications directly to Brightdesk leadership.

actors.name: Lisa Park
actors.summary: Handled VP escalation, investigated team handoffs, and ensured resolution in 4.2.4.

events.title: Nightly CSV export failure reported
events.detail: Hannah Lee reported that nightly CSV exports to Snowflake failed, delivering headers only and blocking finance reconciliation.

events.title: Issue reproduced and logged as P3
events.detail: Minh Tran reproduced empty exports on staging and logged a P3 bug ticket SUP-4812.

events.title: Root cause identified and scheduled post-sprint
events.detail: Ravi Kumar identified 4.2 scheduler timezone migration as cause and scheduled work after sprint end on Oct 1.

events.title: Client escalates due to manual workload
events.detail: Hannah Lee emailed Sarah Okafor stating finance spends 3 hours daily on manual reconciliation workarounds.

events.title: Friday fix promised to client
events.detail: Sarah Okafor assured Hannah Lee that engineering would have a fix deployed by Friday, Sept 26.

events.title: Unverified timeline flagged without priority bump
events.detail: Ravi Kumar warned Friday was unrealistic for a P3 bug, but Sarah Okafor failed to bump ticket priority.

events.title: Handover omits active export issue
events.detail: Sarah Okafor went OOO without including the open export issue in her coverage handover to Tom Becker.

events.title: Promised Friday deadline missed without notice
events.detail: The promised Sept 26 fix did not occur and the ticket remained without updates over the weekend.

events.title: Manual export workaround provided
events.detail: Minh Tran instructed Hannah Lee to run manual exports via UI as a temporary workaround.

events.title: Fix pulled forward into 4.2.3 release
events.detail: Ravi Kumar pulled the bug forward into hotfix 4.2.3 scheduled for release on Thursday, Oct 2.

events.title: PR pulled from release due to test failure
events.detail: PR #2291 failed DST integration tests and was removed from release candidate 4.2.3.

events.title: Release 4.2.3 deployed without export fix
events.detail: Release 4.2.3 shipped to production without the export fix included.

events.title: Incorrect status communicated to client
events.detail: Tom Becker incorrectly assured Hannah Lee that the fix had deployed in release 4.2.3.

events.title: VP Finance escalates to VP Customer Success
events.detail: Daniel Reyes escalated two weeks of failures and contradicting communication to Lisa Park, conditioning renewal on resolution.

events.title: VP CS commits to release 4.2.4 fix
events.detail: Lisa Park apologized, committing to a full timeline call and fix deployment in 4.2.4.

events.title: Release 4.2.4 ships with export fix
events.detail: Release 4.2.4 deployed containing PR #2291 to correct export timezone behavior.

events.title: Scheduled export succeeds
events.detail: Hannah Lee confirmed that the scheduled nightly export completed with 41,233 rows.

events.title: Ticket closed and reclassified to P1
events.detail: Minh Tran marked SUP-4812 resolved and retroactively reclassified it as P1 for SLA review.

commitments.what: Update client daily until ticket SUP-4812 is resolved
commitments.statusReason: Updates lapsed between Sept 24 and Sept 29, leaving the client without status responses [T3, E4, T5].

commitments.what: Have fix in place by Friday, Sept 26
commitments.statusReason: Fix was not delivered by Sept 26 because ticket remained P3 in backlog [C5, T4, E4].

commitments.what: Personally keep Hannah posted on progress
commitments.statusReason: Sarah went on leave without updating the client or listing the ticket in handover [E3, E5, C13].

commitments.what: Sort out ticket priority and timeline with engineering
commitments.statusReason: Sarah failed to reprioritize the ticket, leaving it as P3 in engineering backlog [C6, C13].

commitments.what: Ship fix in hotfix 4.2.3 on Thursday, Oct 2
commitments.statusReason: PR #2291 failed DST tests and was pulled from 4.2.3 release [C9, C10, T9].

commitments.what: Claimed fix was deployed on Oct 2 as part of 4.2.3
commitments.statusReason: PR was pulled from 4.2.3 prior to release, so fix was not deployed [C9, C11, E7, C14].

commitments.what: Provide full timeline call, ship fix in 4.2.4, and confirm successful export
commitments.statusReason: Fix shipped in release 4.2.4 on Oct 7 [C16] and successful export was confirmed Oct 8 [T11].

phases.name: Report and Misaligned Commitment
phases.summary: Northwind reported empty CSV exports impacting billing. Support logged the issue as P3 while Account Management promised a Sept 26 fix without updating engineering priority.

phases.name: Missed Commitment and Handover Gap
phases.summary: The promised Friday fix was missed. Account management went OOO without listing the issue in handover, while engineering pulled the ticket forward for an Oct 2 hotfix.

phases.name: Release Pull and False Confirmation
phases.summary: The fix was pulled from release 4.2.3 due to a test failure, but covering account management falsely assured Northwind that the fix had deployed.

phases.name: Executive Escalation and Resolution
phases.summary: Northwind's VP Finance escalated the failure. Engineering shipped the fix in release 4.2.4 on Oct 7, and the export was verified working on Oct 8.

whatWentWrong.title: Unauthorized Timeline Commitments and Priority Misalignment
whatWentWrong.detail: Support logged a billing-blocking issue as a P3 bug [T2]. Account Manager Sarah Okafor committed to a Sept 26 fix with the client [E2] despite engineering explicitly stating the ticket was in the backlog until Oct 1 [C2, C5]. No internal priority bump was requested or executed [C6, C13].

whatWentWrong.title: Unverified Release Confirmation to Client
whatWentWrong.detail: When PR #2291 failed DST tests and was pulled from release 4.2.3 [C9], covering Account Manager Tom Becker told Northwind the fix had deployed [E7] based on milestone tagging without verifying actual release notes or confirmation from engineering [C14].

whatWentWrong.title: Account Handover and Support Communication Gaps
whatWentWrong.detail: Sarah Okafor went on leave without including Northwind's ongoing export issue in her OOO handover [E3, C13]. Furthermore, support ticket communications lapsed between Sept 24 and Sept 29, leaving the client without updates after missing the promised deadline [T3, T5, E4].

contradictions.title: Promised Sept 26 Fix Date vs. Post-Sprint Backlog Status
contradictions.detail: Sarah Okafor told Northwind on Sept 23 that a fix would be in place by Friday, Sept 26 [E2]. Internally, engineering had assigned the ticket to P3 backlog status scheduled after Oct 1 [C2] and expressly warned that Friday was unrealistic without a priority change [C5].

contradictions.title: Deployed Status Claim vs. Pulled Release Candidate
contradictions.detail: Tom Becker informed Northwind on Oct 3 that the fix shipped on Oct 2 in release 4.2.3 [E7]. In reality, PR #2291 was pulled from 4.2.3 on Oct 2 due to integration test failures [C9] and was omitted from the release [C11].

openQuestions: Why was a bug directly blocking daily finance reconciliation initially triaged as P3 without evaluating financial workflow impact?
What process exists between release management and account management to ensure customer-facing teams do not claim feature deployment based on milestone tagging alone?
Why was ticket SUP-4812 left without updates between Sept 24 and Sept 29 despite daily update commitments?
clientReply: Dear Daniel, I sincerely apologize for the unacceptable communication failures and resolution delays regarding your nightly CSV exports over the past two weeks. You should never have had to resort to manual workarounds or receive contradictory statements from our team. On September 23, we promised a resolution date of September 26 without aligning engineering priorities. Later, on October 3, we incorrectly informed you that the fix was deployed in release 4.2.3 when it had actually been pulled due to a late test failure. I am glad to confirm that release 4.2.4 deployed successfully on October 7, and your scheduled export on October 8 completed with all 41,233 records. To prevent this from recurring, we have updated our triage policy so issues impacting critical financial workflows are automatically treated as Priority 1. Additionally, we are introducing a strict release verification workflow requiring sign-off from release management before customer success confirms fixes. I look forward to speaking with you today to discuss accountability and our partnership moving forward.
